output.title: What folder structure usually hides in a small business
output.body:
For an owner-run small business, messy folders usually point to a simpler problem: repeated document search. If you keep hunting for customer agreements, invoices, contracts, or past decisions, the folder tree is not the workflow. It is where the friction shows up.

The bounded decision is not “reorganise everything.” It is: is the next automation effort worth starting only after you can name one repeatable document task that matters, such as invoice filing, contract retrieval, or answering a customer query from old files? That is a threshold question, not a full system rebuild.

A practical next step is manual: pick your most common lookup and track it for one week. Each time it happens, note three things: what you were looking for, which folders you checked, and how long it took before you found it or gave up. That is not glamorous work. It is just the sort of thing that tells you whether you have occasional clutter or a recurring process.

If the same lookup keeps coming back and takes real time, there may be a workflow worth tightening. If it is ad hoc or takes seconds, the folder structure may be annoying, but not yet a business process. Folder names are often the smoke, not the fire.
